name: Nitroglycerin
summary: A rapid-acting nitrate that relieves acute angina within minutes via nitric oxide-mediated venodilation and reduced myocardial oxygen demand.
mechanism: Donates nitric oxide, which activates vascular smooth muscle guanylate cyclase and raises cGMP, causing venodilation (reduced preload), arterial dilation, and coronary vasodilation.
targets: Vascular smooth muscle guanylate cyclase (via NO)
pharmacodynamics: Reduces preload and myocardial oxygen demand; relieves ischemic pain within minutes when given sublingually.

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Rapid hepatic and vascular metabolism by organic nitrate reductase (denitration)

dosing.adult: Acute angina: 0.3–0.6 mg sublingually, repeat every 5 min up to 3 doses; IV infusion 10–20 mcg/min titrated; transdermal patch 0.2–0.8 mg/h with a daily nitrate-free interval

safety.pregnancy: Use only if clearly needed (no adequate data)
contraindications: Concomitant PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil, vardenafil) — severe hypotension
warnings: Severe hypotension, especially with PDE5 inhibitors
safety.overdose: Severe hypotension; supportive care; consider methylene blue for methemoglobinemia

indications: Long-term angina prevention (patch/ointment with nitrate-free interval)
clinicalPearls: Take at the first sign of angina; if pain persists after three sublingual doses, seek emergency care.
A 10–12 h nitrate-free interval prevents tolerance.
good: Immediate symptom relief for exertional or unstable angina.
bad: Patients on PDE5 inhibitors or with hypotension; not for chronic monotherapy without a nitrate-free interval.
